rows.title: Judge Orders Twitter To Unmask FBI Impersonator Who Set Off Seth Rich Conspiracy
rows.standfirst: A federal judge has ordered Twitter to reveal the identity of an anonymous user who allegedly forged an FBI document to spread a conspiracy theory about the killing of DNC staffer Seth Rich in 2016.

rows.title: Facebook Vows To Crack Down On Voter Intimidation In Election
rows.standfirst: The social network announced new measures to prevent misinformation, threats and confusion surrounding the election, but said it would let Donald Trump Jr's call for an 'army of poll watchers' stand.

rows.title: The Great Fridge Freeze-Out
rows.standfirst: For months now, there's been a shortage of refrigerators and freezers across the U.S. Shoppers can't find appliances to buy and stores can't find enough appliances to sell. Alina Selyukh joins The Indicator to explain why.

rows.title: Rethinking Black Wealth
rows.standfirst: Homes in Black neighborhoods are valued lower than homes in white neighborhoods. Why? This episode, Dr. Andre Perry flips the narrative of the racial wealth gap. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: A PBR Seltzer Spiked With THC Hits Shelves, Aiming At The 'Canna-Curious'
rows.standfirst: While a THC seltzer may seem like a niche product, it's actually part of a larger pattern, as big companies try to learn more about a part of the cannabis market that could see explosive growth.

rows.title: Airlines, Travel Groups Warn Of More Job Cuts As COVID-19 Aid Talks Stall
rows.standfirst: With tens of thousands already out of work, travel industry groups warn another 1.3 million jobs could be lost if Congress and the White House fail to reach agreement on coronavirus relief soon.

rows.title: It's Not Goodbye, But Not Good Either: Ruby Tuesday Declares Bankruptcy
rows.standfirst: The chain does "not intend to reopen 185 of their restaurants that were closed during the pandemic," Ruby Tuesday's CEO wrote in a court filing.

rows.title: McAfee Founder Accused Of Evading Taxes While Allegedly Earning Millions
rows.standfirst: John McAfee was arrested in Spain and now faces extradition to the U.S. Prosecutors say he didn't file tax returns from 2014 to 2018, and concealed millions of dollars through various methods.

rows.title: Stocks Surge After White House Says It's Open To Pandemic Aid After All
rows.standfirst: Stocks reversed Tuesday's losses amid word that the Trump administration was considering stand-alone bills to aid airlines and small businesses. The president had called off talks on a relief bill.

rows.title: White House Eyes Piecemeal Pandemic Aid After Trump Ends Talks On Overall Package
rows.standfirst: But a top aide to Speaker Nancy Pelosi tweeted that she spoke to the treasury secretary Wednesday about a standalone measure to help airlines. A previous attempt to do this failed amid GOP opposition.

rows.title: Google And Oracle's Decade-Long Copyright Battle Reaches Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: Oracle accuses Google of illegally copying its software. Google contends the kind of code it used cannot be owned by anyone.

rows.title: FDA Releases Long-Awaited COVID-19 Vaccine Guidance
rows.standfirst: The requirements laid out by the Food and Drug Administration in advice for drugmakers underscore why it's unlikely a vaccine could clear the agency before Election Day.

rows.title: Stocks Slump After Trump Halts Coronavirus Stimulus Talks Until After Election
rows.standfirst: Airlines, which have been counting on aid from Congress, were hit hard. Tech shares, which have been among the top gainers this year, also posted losses.

rows.title: How Are Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google Monopolies? House Report Counts The Ways
rows.standfirst: House Democrats recommend Congress look at ways to force the companies to split off some of their businesses, saying the tech giants have exploited their power to benefit themselves and hurt rivals.

rows.title: The Semiconductor Standoff
rows.standfirst: As the trade war continues, China hasn't purchased nearly as many exports from the United States as it previously agreed to. There was one bright spot though: semiconductors — but that may soon change.

rows.title: Facebook And Twitter Limit Sharing 'New York Post' Story About Joe Biden
rows.standfirst: The social media companies said they wanted to slow the spread of possibly false information. But their actions drew charges of censorship from President Trump and his allies.

rows.title: Daymond John Plays Overrated Or Underrated
rows.standfirst: Daymond John and what he thinks is overrated and what's underrated

rows.title: Caste Arrives In Silicon Valley
rows.standfirst: For some Indian employees of big U.S. tech companies, caste discrimination is real. To combat it, first people have to talk about it. That's hard. | Today's episode is from our friends at Rough Translation.

rows.title: Why An Auto Plant Closure Looms Large In Presidential Contest In Ohio
rows.standfirst: In 2016, support for Donald Trump surged in northeast Ohio. But the 2019 closure of General Motors' plant in Lordstown may have changed residents' views.

rows.title: Judge Blocks Wisconsin Governor's Indoor Capacity Limits Amid Spike In COVID-19 Cases
rows.standfirst: The rules issued last week limited indoor public gatherings to no more than 25% of total occupancy limits. The state's Tavern League argued the caps would effectively put its members out of business.

rows.title: Power Of The Petition: Nonprofit Helps Front-Line Workers Fight For Their Rights
rows.standfirst: Eight out of every nine American workers don't have a union to represent them in workplace disputes. A nonprofit website is helping push for better wages and working conditions amid the pandemic.

rows.title: Time To Ditch Those Awful Zoom Calls, CEOs Say
rows.standfirst: Draining. Awful. Those are the words being used to describe virtual meetings. "What we as human beings need, want, seek ... is human contact," says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.

rows.title: 'So Hard To Prove You Exist': Flawed Fraud Protections Deny Unemployment To Millions
rows.standfirst: Efforts to prevent fraud in state unemployment systems are outdated, hurting millions of people with legitimate claims by causing lengthy and unnecessary delays while not managing to catch much fraud.

rows.title: Delta Loses $5 Billion In 3rd Quarter, May Soon Furlough 1,700 Pilots
rows.standfirst: Delta is the first major airline to report 3rd quarter results and lost more than expected, as air travel demand remains weak due to the pandemic.

rows.title: How Vikings Launched Globalization 1.0
rows.standfirst: How the Vikings trading with a North American Indigenous group shortly after the year 1000 connected global trading networks and kicked off the first version of globalization.

rows.title: Apple Unveils iPhone 12 With 5G, But Most Won't Feel Faster Speeds Anytime Soon
rows.standfirst: Eventually, smartphones with 5G capabilities could be up to 20 times faster than the current 4G standard, but most places in the U.S. still don't have the infrastructure to support 5G.

rows.title: Front-Line Workers Use Online Tools And Public Shaming To Fight For Fairer Workplace
rows.standfirst: Front-line workers at grocery and retail stores have been flocking to a nonprofit site, Coworker.org, to make demands such as better pay and better schedules — with a fair degree of success.

rows.title: Facebook Bans Ads Discouraging Vaccines, In Latest Misinformation Crackdown
rows.standfirst: The move is a reversal of Facebook's longstanding reluctance to block problematic content. Critics say public health misinformation has flourished on the social network.

rows.title: Johnson & Johnson, Eli Lilly Pause COVID-19 Drug Trials
rows.standfirst: The move by Eli Lilly came less than 24 hours after Johnson & Johnson paused further dosing in all of its COVID-19 vaccine candidate clinical trials while it investigated a volunteer's illness.

rows.title: Trouble On Main Street
rows.standfirst: The Federal Reserve launched a massive program to lend to small and midsize businesses. It has hardly loaned out anything.

rows.title: Hey Google, Are You Too Big?
rows.standfirst: The government just filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google. In this episode, we talk about why, and why it matters. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Quibi, Short-Form Streaming Service, Shutting Down
rows.standfirst: It was an abrupt ending — just six months after launch — for a company founded by big names in the entertainment and business worlds.

rows.title: Arkansas AG On Google Antitrust Suit: 'I Don't Want What Google Says Is Best'
rows.standfirst: Arkansas Attorney General Leslie Rutledge describes the reasoning behind the antitrust lawsuit against Google filed by the Justice Department and 11 state attorneys general.

rows.title: How Will The Limited Supply Of Antibody Drugs For COVID-19 Be Allocated?
rows.standfirst: Experimental medicines have the potential to help people with COVID-19 avoid hospitalization. The scarce supply of the treatments would have to be rationed, if regulators OK their use.

rows.title: Hope Vs. Despair
rows.standfirst: Should we feel hope or despair about the future of the American economy? Cardiff and Stacey debate.

rows.title: GM Reintroduces Hummer As Fully Electric Truck, 1st Model Will Sell For $112,595
rows.standfirst: The Hummer EV will go on sale in fall 2021. Known previously for its gas inefficiency, the new Hummer will now run completely on electricity.

rows.title: Google Lawsuit Marks End Of Washington's Love Affair With Big Tech
rows.standfirst: The Justice Department's lawsuit against Google is the clearest sign yet of the "Techlash" that has politicians on both sides of the aisle bristling at the power of Silicon Valley.

rows.title: Oil Jobs Are Big Risk, Big Pay. Green Energy Offers Stability And Passion
rows.standfirst: Workers in the energy sector face two paths: The oil industry offers big salaries but more volatility, while clean energy pays less but provides more stability and a sense of mission.

rows.title: Purdue Pharma Reaches $8B Opioid Deal With Justice Department Over OxyContin Sales
rows.standfirst: Critics say the settlement doesn't hold company executives or members of the Sackler family accountable for their aggressive marketing of OxyContin, which helped fuel the nation's opioid epidemic.

rows.title: Why Women Are Leaving The Workforce
rows.standfirst: Of the 1.1 million people who left the job market in September, over 860,000 were women. Today we look at why women are dropping out of the workforce and what it will mean for the economy.

rows.title: Even The Most Successful Women Pay A Big Price
rows.standfirst: The unequal division of household work leads to the "mom penalty." For highly educated, high-income women, it could mean losing promotions, future earning power and roles as future leaders.

rows.title: Rush Limbaugh Says His Lung Cancer Is Terminal, Going In 'Wrong Direction'
rows.standfirst: "Stage 4 is, as they say, terminal," the conservative radio host said. Limbaugh added that after receiving the cancer diagnosis, "I never thought I would see October 1st."

rows.title: Google Abuses Its Monopoly Power Over Search, Justice Department Says In Lawsuit
rows.standfirst: The antitrust lawsuit against Google is the most significant action the federal government has taken against a technology company in two decades. Google calls the lawsuit "deeply flawed."

rows.title: Amid Pandemic, Here's What Researchers Have Learned About The Economy
rows.standfirst: Since COVID-19 hit our shores, economists have been crunching data to see how it's affecting our economy.

rows.title: The Affordable Care Act's Fate Is In Flux But 2021 Health Plan Prices Are Stable
rows.standfirst: The Affordable Care Act's future is uncertain and there's no end in sight to the pandemic. But for the 2021 insurance year consumers can expect to see modest increases in prices, if any.

rows.title: The American Government Once Offered Widely Affordable Child Care ... 77 Years Ago
rows.standfirst: Affordable, quality child care was hard to come by even before the pandemic and now even more so. It's not for a lack of ideas about how to fix it. Is this the moment those ideas are taken seriously?

rows.title: Trump's Ban On TikTok Suffers Another Legal Setback
rows.standfirst: A federal judge put the brakes on yet another aspect of President Trump's push to ban TikTok, but uncertainty still clouds the future of the viral video app in the U.S.

rows.title: Now That More Americans Can Work From Anywhere, Many Are Planning To Move Away
rows.standfirst: Since more people are working from home, they're using the opportunity to migrate to other places. Big cities are seeing the biggest outflows, according to new surveys.

rows.title: What Economy Are You Voting For?
rows.standfirst: Two candidates. Two very different ways of thinking about the economy. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Cruise Lines Can Sail Again From The U.S., But It's Not Clear How Soon
rows.standfirst: The federal government has given the go-ahead for cruise ships to sail from ports in the United States. Officials stopped cruise lines in March as the coronavirus pandemic ramped up.

rows.title: What Is Trumponomics?
rows.standfirst: Danielle Kurtzleben from NPR's Washington Desk breaks down Donald Trump's economic policies and plans for a second term.

rows.title: In Reversal, Walmart Puts Guns Back On Display
rows.standfirst: Walmart is returning guns and ammunition back to display shelves after earlier citing "isolated civil unrest" as the reason for temporarily taking them out of view as a safety precaution.

rows.title: How Are You Surviving In The Pandemic Economy? Share Your Story
rows.standfirst: It's been more than eight months since the COVID-19 pandemic hit the U.S. economy like a wrecking ball. Millions are still out of work. How has it affected your job, your finances and your family?

rows.title: Black And Latino Voters Flooded With Disinformation In Election's Final Days
rows.standfirst: Hoaxes and misleading posts aimed at depressing turnout have spread on social media. Experts say it outpaces 2016, when Black voters were the top target of Russian-backed disinformation.

rows.title: Walmart Yanks Guns Off Shelves Citing Rising Tensions
rows.standfirst: The retail giant removed firearms and ammunition from its shelves saying it's a precautionary step amid the recent outbreak of civil unrest. But the weapons are still available, if you ask for them.

rows.title: What Is Bidenomics?
rows.standfirst: Danielle Kurtzleben from NPR's Washington Desk breaks down Joe Biden's economic policies.

rows.title: U.S. Economy Grows At Record Pace But Still Has A Long Way To Go
rows.standfirst: U.S. GDP grew at a record 33.1% annualized pace in the third quarter, erasing some but not all of the damage done by the coronavirus recession.

rows.title: Pandemic Means Closing Time For Many New York City Restaurants And Bars
rows.standfirst: Cold temps added to rising debts are forcing New York City restaurants to close or reinvent themselves for the pandemic era.

rows.title: New GDP Numbers Won't Be Enough To Repair All Economic Damage
rows.standfirst: The Commerce Department reported record-setting economic growth during the most recent quarter. But the economy is far from healthy, after a record-shattering collapse earlier this year.

rows.title: Citing 'Devastating' Pandemic Impact, Boeing To Lay Off 7,000 More Workers
rows.standfirst: "This moment is among the most difficult in our more than 100-year history," CEO Dave Calhoun said. Most of the layoffs will be in Washington state, where Boeing designs and builds many aircraft.
